comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum page defines a three-year, 180-EC bachelor organised as four blocks of two courses per year and says the current public course list is indicative. Year one comprises eight compulsory 7.5-EC foundations (60 EC). In years two and three students choose from category-based chemistry offerings and free choices, complete the compulsory Anorganische & Vastestofchemie course and finish with a 15-EC ten-week individual bachelor research project. The generic target names neither of the two official study paths, so the first-listed Moleculen en Materialen path is selected by neutral official order. A coherent 105-EC set of fourteen 7.5-EC post-first-year courses is instantiated from the published materials, physical, inorganic, analytical and supporting-methods offerings; the 15-EC thesis completes the later 120 EC. The linked one-page visual schedule is still labelled 2025–26, while the live public curriculum page was checked on 2026-09-28 and is treated as the current source; the public page warns that offerings may change.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names neither official study path. Moleculen en Materialen is listed before Moleculen en Leven on the current curriculum page, so it is selected neutrally before UCR fit is considered. The concrete pathway uses a coherent set of published materials, physical, inorganic, analytical and supporting-methods courses while satisfying the displayed category structure.

exception.reason: Utrecht Chemistry is defined by a compulsory first-year sequence in organic chemistry and spectroscopy, physical and inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, quantum chemistry, mathematics and physics, with extensive laboratory work. The selected Molecules and Materials pathway continues through physical, inorganic, solid-state, electrochemical, structural, spectroscopic, catalytic, organometallic, polymer, nano- and surface chemistry and ends in an individual chemistry research project. UCR has no chemistry gateway and no stand-alone progression in organic, inorganic, analytical, physical, quantum or synthetic chemistry. A 24-course UCR programme could combine biochemistry, environmental science, sustainability, mathematics and programming, but it would omit the target’s defining chemistry theory and multi-laboratory spine and would therefore misrepresent the degree.
exception.curriculumContext: The current public curriculum and its linked visual schedule account for exactly 180 EC: eight 7.5-EC compulsory first-year courses (60 EC), fourteen selected 7.5-EC post-first-year courses (105 EC), and a 15-EC ten-week individual bachelor thesis project. The first-listed Molecules and Materials path is instantiated with courses in molecular modelling, physical and organic chemistry, compulsory inorganic/solid-state chemistry, electrochemistry, structure determination, spectroscopy, catalysis, nanomaterials, organometallic and polymer chemistry, solids and surfaces, plus biochemical research methods. The live page is current as checked on 2026-09-28; its linked visual schedule remains labelled 2025–26 and the page cautions that offerings can change.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide biomolecular content and one broad biochemical/molecular laboratory course. HCBGATE101 and HCBLIFE211 cover cells and molecular life science. ENSGATE101/201 contain some general physics, chemistry and materials-science foundations; ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry and ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation touch geochemical or inorganic processes and resource recovery; ENSSUST112 addresses life-cycle and circular-economy analysis. DISGATE102 and DISGATE101 supply mathematical and programming support. None provides a disciplinary chemistry sequence in organic synthesis, inorganic and solid-state chemistry, analytical measurement, thermodynamics and physical chemistry, quantum chemistry, molecular spectroscopy, catalysis, electrochemistry or materials characterisation, nor a progressive set of chemistry laboratories. These isolated biochemical, environmental and sustainability offerings cannot support 23 non-PPD courses with concrete relevance to a Chemistry concept or prepare a student for the target’s independent chemistry research project.
